title: Walking a range
hints: `begin` points at the first element and `end` points one **past** the last. Move a pointer from `begin` toward `end`, one element at a time with `p++`.
Loop `for (const int *p = begin; p != end; p++)`. The element under the pointer is `*p`. Never dereference `end` itself: it isn't part of the range.
`long total = 0; for (const int *p = begin; p != end; p++) { if (*p > limit) total += *p; } return total;`
